subject: International discovery recap — proposed evals, model shortlist, and pilot action plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Helena Möller <helena.moller@linguatech.com>, Marco Tan <marco.tan@scribo.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: International discovery recap — proposed evals, model shortlist, and pilot action plan

Hi Helena / Marco —

Thanks for the intro call earlier today. Short recap and clear next steps below so we keep momentum. I captured the items we discussed and our recommended path to validate model fit across your EU product languages (DE, FR, NL, ES) and APAC targets (JA, KO, ZH-HK).

What we heard (high level):
- Core flows: translation + user-facing summarization of support content, and a short-answer assistant embedded in the web console.
- Quality tolerances: DE must preserve formality for enterprise customers; JA requires polite registers and correct honorifics.
- Non-functional: < 250ms median token latency for interactive queries; on-prem data residency preferred for EU PII in Q2 pilot.

Redwood recommendations (model shortlist for pilot):
1) redwood-intl-xlarge-v2 (primary) — strong EU multilingual performance, robust for formal/informal register controls.
2) rwl-13b-q4-multilang (fallback for cost-sensitive batches) — good throughput, watch regen on complex DE morphology.
3) redwood-7b-asia-tuned (APAC candidate) — optimized tokenization for JA/KO, lower memory footprint for private deployment.

Quick regression & risk notes:
- German: past evals show regressions with machine-translation-style literalism when prompts omit register markers. We recommend a focused prompt/bias set and a targeted evaluation rubric.
- Japanese: KV-cache tokenization differences can affect polite endings; include 3-4 canonical dialogue prompts to validate.

What I'm sending you now (attachments + links):
- prompt_set_LinguaTech_v1.json (sample prompt templates and instruction wrappers for each flow)
- benchmarks_summary_20280310.pdf (internal runbook of token-level latency and quality scores across the shortlist)
- mutual_action_plan_LinguaTech.xlsx (proposed pilot scope, success metrics, timeline, and responsibilities)
- Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/Shared/benchmarks/LinguaTech-20280310

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
- Confirm pilot scope and target languages (we suggest DE, FR, JA initial trifecta) — action: LinguaTech (Helena)
- Approve model shortlist and whether you want Hosted API pilot vs Private deployment trial (data residency) — action: LinguaTech
- Redwood to run a 2-week eval using your sample corpus + our prompt_set; we’ll produce per-language regression reports and a final recommendation — action: Redwood (Neha + Aditya)
- Share any procurement/PO constraints — action: LinguaTech (Marco)

If you confirm scope today, we can kick off the eval by next Tuesday and aim to deliver the readout in 3 weeks.

Best,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: International discovery recap — proposed evals, model shortlist, and pilot action plan

Thanks Neha —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying points from our side before we lock scope: 

- Languages: We definitely want DE and JA. FR is lower priority; could substitute ES instead for the first pass if that simplifies dataset prep.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in our EU tenant for the pilot. Can Redwood support a Private deployment inside our GCP EU project (preferred) or a Hosted EU region with contractually-scoped logs retention?
- Benchmarks: Can you highlight which metrics in the PDF we should focus on to evaluate DE formality and JA politeness?

We will assemble a 2k-sentence sample set for DE and JA keyed for formality registers and honorific usage by the end of this week. Marco — I’ll need the procurement timelines; any constraints?

Also: any quick wins to reduce visible failure modes? For example, we need guardrails on hallucination in the summarization flow (high cost to support).

On the attachments: I see the prompt set file — will review and loop back with comments.

Best,
Helena
Head of Localization, LinguaTech
helena.moller@linguatech.com

Subject: Re: International discovery recap — proposed evals, model shortlist, and pilot action plan

Helena — thanks, great questions. Quick answers and clarifications below.

Deployment & residency:
- Private deployment: yes, we can run the pilot inside your GCP EU project via our Redwood Private package (customer-managed VPC). Tech notes and a short onboarding checklist are in the attached MAP.
- Hosted EU region: available as an alternative but requires a limited logs-retention SLA change; we can add contractual language for EU-only retention if you prefer faster time-to-value.

Benchmarks highlights to watch (from benchmarks_summary_20280310.pdf):
- DE formality score: we compute BLEU-like edit-distance on a curated register set; redwood-intl-xlarge-v2 hits 91/100 on our formality rubric vs 78/100 for rwl-13b-q4 on sampled enterprise content.
- JA politeness precision: redwood-7b-asia-tuned shows a 94% correct honorific usage on our test set; other models dip into the 80–86% range.
- Hallucination: summarization Factuality metric (ROUGE+entity-precision) shows redwood-intl-xlarge-v2 > other candidates by ~8 points on support-article summarization.

Mitigations & quick wins:
- Prompt engineering: include explicit register tokens (e.g., "Formal-DE: true" / "Polite-JA: true") — sample wrappers in prompt_set_LinguaTech_v1.json.
- Post-filtering: simple NER-based entity verification step for the summarization flow to suppress improbable facts.
- Rolling canary: run the first 20% of live traffic through the pilot models and compare outputs to production; automatic fallback to baseline if the Factuality delta > 10 points.

Proposed pilot scope (from MAP):
- Duration: 3 weeks (2-week eval + 1-week integration/QA)
- Languages: DE, JA, ES (Helena can confirm swap FR/ES)
- Deliverables: per-language regression report, token-latency profile, prompt-set tuning recommendations, model recommendation for GA
- Success criteria: DE formality >= 88/100; JA honorific precision >= 92%; median token latency < 300ms for interactive queries on private deployment config

Please confirm the pilot language set and preferred deployment type (Private in GCP EU vs Hosted EU region). Once you confirm, we will schedule the eval and provide an NDA + pilot SOW for signatures.

Thanks — looping Evelyn to begin CS planning assuming pilot goes ahead.

Neha
